newsitem.title: USA: Bergen stock down on merger concerns.
newsitem.headline: Bergen stock down on merger concerns.

text.p: Shares of drug wholesaler Bergen Brunswig Corp fell sharply amid concerns a merger with generic drug maker IVAX Corp could shift its steady double-digit growth record into a slower gear, analysts said.
An added concern, they said, was that some drug suppliers would be less willing to do business with Bergen once it had a lower-cost in house supplier of generic drugs.
Shares of Bergen Brunswig were down 4-1/4 to 28-1/2. IVAX, which Bergen plans to acquire in a tax-free stock swap deal valued at $1.65 billion, fell 3-1/8 to 12-3/4.

"I think (Bergen) may have done better to wait a year," said Robert Wasserman, an analyst with Southeast Research Partners. Wasserman noted that IVAX was a company in the midst of a restructuring that lost money in its third quarter, and he questioned whether Bergen Brunswig had the expertise to guide IVAX through the overhaul and cost-cuts that would be needed to get it back on track.

"I think there is a lot of concern that Brunswig's other suppliers might be scratching their heads and saying 'Do we really want to do as much business with them now that they have acquired a big drug company?'" added another analyst who asked not to be named.

That analyst added, "It would be good if IVAX could literally supply them with all their drugs; but Bergen buys $2 billion worth of drugs a year, and even if IVAX gave them (Bergen) everything (it produced), it would only be 25 percent of their needs."
